questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest type of cardiomyopathy is:
questions.concept: Dilated cardiomyopathy accounts for the majority of cases and presents with biventricular systolic failure and a globally dilated, poorly contracting heart. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the commonest inherited form.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The systolic murmur of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy increases in intensity with:
questions.concept: Valsalva reduces venous return and left ventricular cavity size, worsening dynamic outflow obstruction and intensifying the murmur. Squatting, leg raising and handgrip all increase preload or afterload and soften it - the reverse of aortic stenosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is most commonly inherited as:
questions.concept: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is autosomal dominant with variable penetrance, most often from mutations in beta-myosin heavy chain (MYH7) or myosin-binding protein C. First-degree relatives should be screened.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest congenital heart disease overall is:
questions.concept: Ventricular septal defect is the commonest congenital cardiac malformation. Tetralogy of Fallot is the commonest cyanotic lesion beyond infancy and bicuspid aortic valve the commonest congenital valve anomaly.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest cyanotic congenital heart disease beyond one year of age is:
questions.concept: Tetralogy of Fallot is the commonest cyanotic lesion surviving beyond infancy, while transposition of the great arteries is the commonest presenting in the neonatal period. Squatting relieves cyanosis by raising systemic vascular resistance.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A wide and fixed split second heart sound is characteristic of:
questions.concept: Fixed wide splitting of the second sound results from the constant right ventricular volume overload of an atrial septal defect, which abolishes the normal respiratory variation. Pulmonary stenosis causes wide but still variable splitting.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A continuous machinery murmur best heard in the left infraclavicular area suggests:
questions.concept: A patent ductus arteriosus produces a continuous machinery murmur because the aorta-to-pulmonary artery pressure gradient persists through systole and diastole, with a wide pulse pressure and bounding pulses.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A cyanosed infant has pink upper limbs with cyanosed lower limbs (differential cyanosis). The likely lesion is:
options: Patent ductus arteriosus with shunt reversal
questions.concept: Differential cyanosis sparing the upper body occurs when deoxygenated pulmonary artery blood enters the aorta distal to the left subclavian through a reversed ductus, as in severe pulmonary hypertension or a duct-dependent coarctation. Intracardiac shunts cause uniform cyanosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy worldwide is:
questions.concept: Cardiac amyloidosis is the commonest cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy, showing a speckled myocardium with low-voltage ECG despite thick walls. Endomyocardial fibrosis is important in tropical regions but is less frequent overall.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Which drug is contraindicated in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy?
questions.concept: Digoxin increases contractility and therefore worsens dynamic outflow tract obstruction; diuretics, nitrates and vasodilators are similarly harmful. Beta blockers, verapamil and disopyramide are negatively inotropic and are the mainstay of treatment.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia is:
questions.concept: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the single commonest identified cause of community-acquired pneumonia, typically producing lobar consolidation with rusty sputum and a rapid response to amoxicillin.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Which is NOT a component of the CURB-65 severity score?
questions.concept: CURB-65 comprises Confusion, Urea above 7 mmol/L, Respiratory rate 30 or more, Blood pressure below 90/60 mmHg and age 65 or above. Oxygen saturation is not part of the score, although it guides oxygen therapy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A young adult has an atypical pneumonia with cold agglutinins and haemolysis. The likely organism is:
questions.concept: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is associated with cold agglutinin mediated haemolysis, erythema multiforme and bullous myringitis, and radiographic changes exceeding clinical signs. It is treated with a macrolide or doxycycline as it lacks a cell wall.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: In a patient who aspirates while supine, a lung abscess most commonly develops in the:
options: Posterior segment of the right upper lobe
questions.concept: Aspirated material follows gravity into the posterior segment of the right upper lobe or the superior segment of the right lower lobe when supine, favoured by the more vertical right main bronchus.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The investigation of choice for confirming bronchiectasis is:
options: High-resolution computed tomography of the chest
questions.concept: High-resolution CT is the current standard, showing bronchial dilatation with a bronchoarterial ratio above 1, lack of tapering and the signet-ring sign. Bronchography is obsolete.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Kartagener syndrome comprises:
questions.concept: Kartagener syndrome is the triad of situs inversus, bronchiectasis and chronic sinusitis caused by primary ciliary dyskinesia, with immotile sperm producing male infertility.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Thick, blood-tinged currant-jelly sputum in a diabetic alcoholic with an upper lobe cavity suggests:
questions.concept: Klebsiella (Friedlander) pneumonia typically affects diabetics and alcoholics, producing viscid currant-jelly sputum, upper lobe involvement, bulging fissures and a tendency to cavitate.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The most useful rapid diagnostic test for Legionella pneumophila infection is:
questions.concept: Legionella does not stain on routine Gram stain and grows only on buffered charcoal yeast extract medium, so urinary antigen detection is the practical rapid test. Hyponatraemia, diarrhoea and raised transaminases are supportive clues.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: An HIV-positive patient with CD4 count 90 per microlitre has progressive breathlessness, bilateral perihilar infiltrates and a markedly raised lactate dehydrogenase. The likely diagnosis is:
questions.concept: Pneumocystis pneumonia occurs when CD4 falls below 200, causing dry cough, marked hypoxia on exertion, bilateral perihilar ground-glass shadowing and raised LDH. Diagnosis is by silver or immunofluorescent staining of induced sputum or lavage.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The drug of choice for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is:
questions.concept: High-dose cotrimoxazole is first line for both treatment and prophylaxis; adjunctive corticosteroids are added when the arterial oxygen tension is below 70 mmHg. Antifungals are ineffective despite the organism being a fungus.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: By Light's criteria, a pleural fluid to serum protein ratio greater than 0.5 indicates:
questions.concept: Light's criteria classify fluid as exudative if the protein ratio exceeds 0.5, the LDH ratio exceeds 0.6, or pleural LDH exceeds two-thirds of the upper limit of normal serum LDH. Transudates arise from altered hydrostatic or oncotic pressure.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: The commonest cause of an exudative pleural effusion in India is:
questions.concept: Tuberculosis is the leading cause of exudative effusion in India, characteristically lymphocyte-predominant with high adenosine deaminase and low glucose, and pleural biopsy has a higher yield than fluid culture.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: A parapneumonic effusion with pH 7.0, glucose 30 mg/dL and frank pus on aspiration requires:
questions.concept: A complicated parapneumonic effusion or empyema, indicated by pH below 7.2, glucose below 60 mg/dL, high LDH or frank pus, needs prompt intercostal tube drainage in addition to antibiotics.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: The immediate management of a tension pneumothorax is:
questions.concept: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis treated by immediate needle decompression in the second intercostal space in the midclavicular space or the safe triangle, followed by tube drainage. Waiting for a radiograph can be fatal.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: In a massive pleural effusion, the trachea and mediastinum are displaced:
questions.concept: A large effusion is a space-occupying process that pushes the mediastinum away from the affected side, whereas collapse or fibrosis pulls it towards the lesion - the key bedside distinction.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: High-resolution CT showing basal, subpleural reticulation with honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis indicates:
options: Usual interstitial pneumonia pattern of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
questions.concept: Basal and subpleural predominant reticulation with honeycombing defines the usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, which is diagnostic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in the right clinical setting and avoids the need for biopsy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: Exposure to asbestos is most specifically associated with which malignancy?
questions.concept: Malignant pleural mesothelioma is the tumour most specifically linked to asbestos, with a long latency of 20 to 40 years and no relation to smoking, although asbestos also increases bronchogenic carcinoma risk.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: Eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes on a chest radiograph is characteristic of:
questions.concept: Peripheral or eggshell calcification of hilar nodes is classical of silicosis, which also predisposes strongly to tuberculosis (silicotuberculosis). Byssinosis from cotton dust causes no radiographic change.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: The characteristic pulmonary function pattern in interstitial lung disease is:
options: Reduced FEV1 with reduced FEV1/FVC ratio
Normal spirometry with raised residual volume
Reduced FVC with normal or raised FEV1/FVC ratio and reduced DLCO
Raised total lung capacity with reduced DLCO
questions.concept: Interstitial disease is restrictive: total lung capacity and FVC fall while the FEV1 to FVC ratio is preserved or raised, and diffusing capacity falls early, often before radiographic change.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pleural effusion, pneumothorax & interstitial lung disease
questions.stem: The commonest non-traumatic cause of chylothorax is:
questions.concept: Lymphoma is the commonest non-traumatic cause of chylothorax through obstruction of the thoracic duct, while surgical or penetrating injury dominates traumatic cases. The fluid is milky with triglycerides above 110 mg/dL.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The commonest source of a pulmonary embolus is:
options: Deep veins of the lower limb and pelvis
questions.concept: More than 90% of pulmonary emboli arise from deep vein thrombosis of the lower limbs and pelvic veins, particularly the ileofemoral segment, which yields the largest and most dangerous emboli.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The commonest electrocardiographic finding in acute pulmonary embolism is:
questions.concept: Sinus tachycardia is the commonest ECG finding, while the classical S1Q3T3 pattern is uncommon and indicates massive embolism. A normal ECG does not exclude the diagnosis.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The investigation of choice for suspected pulmonary embolism in a haemodynamically stable patient is:
questions.concept: CT pulmonary angiography is the current investigation of choice, directly demonstrating intraluminal filling defects. Ventilation-perfusion scanning is reserved for renal failure, contrast allergy or pregnancy.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The main clinical value of the D-dimer assay in suspected pulmonary embolism is that it:
options: Excludes the diagnosis when normal in a low-probability patient
questions.concept: D-dimer has high sensitivity but poor specificity, so a normal value in a patient with low or intermediate clinical probability effectively excludes venous thromboembolism, whereas a raised value is non-specific and needs imaging.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: A patient with pulmonary embolism has systolic blood pressure of 78 mmHg. The treatment of choice is:
questions.concept: Massive pulmonary embolism with haemodynamic instability is an indication for systemic thrombolysis with alteplase, or surgical or catheter embolectomy if thrombolysis is contraindicated. Anticoagulation alone is insufficient.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: Which is NOT a component of the Wells score for pulmonary embolism?
questions.concept: The Wells score uses clinical features and risk factors including tachycardia, immobilisation or surgery, previous venous thromboembolism, haemoptysis, malignancy and signs of deep vein thrombosis. D-dimer is applied after the score, not within it.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The Westermark sign on chest radiograph in pulmonary embolism refers to:
options: A prominent right descending pulmonary artery
questions.concept: The Westermark sign is regional oligaemia distal to the occluded vessel. The Hampton hump is the peripheral wedge-shaped infarct and the Palla sign the enlarged right descending pulmonary artery.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: Pulmonary hypertension is currently defined by a mean pulmonary artery pressure at rest greater than:
questions.concept: The current haemodynamic definition is a mean pulmonary artery pressure above 20 mmHg at rest on right heart catheterisation, which remains the diagnostic gold standard; pre-capillary disease additionally requires pulmonary vascular resistance of 2 Wood units or more.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The gold standard investigation for obstructive sleep apnoea is:
questions.concept: Polysomnography establishes the diagnosis and grades severity by the apnoea-hypopnoea index: 5 to 15 mild, 15 to 30 moderate and above 30 severe. The Epworth scale only assesses subjective sleepiness.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension & sleep apnoea
questions.stem: The treatment of choice for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea is:
questions.concept: Nasal continuous positive airway pressure splints the upper airway open and is the treatment of choice, reducing daytime sleepiness and cardiovascular risk. Weight reduction is essential adjunctive therapy.
questions.reference: HARR 21e, Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The commonest cause of anaemia worldwide is:
questions.concept: Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional deficiency and cause of anaemia globally, producing a microcytic hypochromic picture with low ferritin, raised total iron binding capacity and low transferrin saturation.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The earliest laboratory indicator of iron deficiency is:
options: Rise in total iron binding capacity
questions.concept: Depletion of iron stores lowers serum ferritin before serum iron, red cell indices or haemoglobin change, making ferritin the earliest and most useful marker. Haemoglobin falls only after stores are exhausted.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Which iron profile is characteristic of anaemia of chronic disease?
options: Low serum iron, high TIBC, low ferritin
Low serum iron, high TIBC, high ferritin
Low serum iron, low TIBC, normal or raised ferritin
High serum iron, low TIBC, high ferritin
questions.concept: In anaemia of chronic disease hepcidin traps iron in macrophages, so serum iron and TIBC are both low while ferritin is normal or raised. Iron deficiency differs by having a high TIBC and low ferritin.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Macrocytic anaemia accompanied by subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord indicates deficiency of:
questions.concept: Only vitamin B12 deficiency causes neurological disease - posterior column and pyramidal tract degeneration and peripheral neuropathy - because B12 is required for myelin maintenance. Folate replacement alone can precipitate or worsen these features.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Which biochemical finding distinguishes vitamin B12 deficiency from folate deficiency?
questions.concept: Methylmalonic acid accumulates only in B12 deficiency because B12 is the cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. Homocysteine rises in both, and hypersegmented neutrophils occur in any megaloblastic process.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A child with anaemia, abdominal colic and basophilic stippling of red cells most likely has:
questions.concept: Lead inhibits ferrochelatase and ALA dehydratase, producing microcytic anaemia with coarse basophilic stippling, abdominal colic, a gum lead line and raised free erythrocyte protoporphyrin.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Sickle cell disease results from substitution of valine for glutamic acid at position 6 of the:
questions.concept: HbS arises from a single point mutation replacing glutamic acid with valine at the sixth residue of the beta globin chain, which polymerises on deoxygenation and deforms the red cell.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A patient has haemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, MCV 62 fL, a normal red cell count of 5.6 million per microlitre and normal serum ferritin. The likely diagnosis is:
questions.concept: Marked microcytosis with a preserved or raised red cell count and normal iron stores indicates thalassaemia trait; the Mentzer index (MCV divided by RBC count) is below 13, whereas iron deficiency gives a value above 13 with a low red cell count.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria is best diagnosed by:
options: Flow cytometry for CD55 and CD59 deficiency
questions.concept: A PIGA mutation causes loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators CD55 and CD59, so flow cytometry demonstrating their deficiency has replaced the older Ham and sucrose lysis tests as the diagnostic standard.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Pancytopenia with a hypocellular bone marrow and no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy suggests:
questions.concept: Aplastic anaemia is pancytopenia with a fatty, hypocellular marrow and characteristically absent organomegaly. Leukaemia and myelofibrosis give a cellular marrow with splenomegaly, and megaloblastic anaemia a hypercellular marrow.
